T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [YES] — shoulder season strategy, climate-driven travel pattern shifts

Synopsis:
Tui reports a 43% drop in pre-tax profits (€153m vs €267m YoY) for Q2 April–June, driven by geopolitical uncertainty (Iran war), cost-of-living pressures, high fuel costs, and a competitive market. Two cruise ships were stranded in the Gulf for 12 weeks at a cost of €40m. Consumer booking behaviour has shifted toward last-minute decisions. Demand has partially recovered in recent weeks. Structurally, Tui is adapting to climate-driven shifts toward shoulder-season travel.
